domain_guidance.summary: This domain covers case selection and management strategies, representing 20.0 percent of the evaluation. It focuses heavily on patient evaluation and therapeutic decision-making for interventional procedures in clinical practice.

This domain focuses on procedural techniques, accounting for 20.0 percent of the total evaluation. It encompasses technical skills, procedural execution methods, and practical applications used during cardiac interventions.

This domain addresses complications of coronary intervention, comprising 8.0 percent of the exam content. It emphasizes the identification, mitigation, and clinical management of adverse events occurring during coronary procedures.

This domain involves catheter-based management of noncoronary disease, making up 13.0 percent of the content. It centers entirely on therapeutic interventions performed outside the primary coronary vasculature.

This domain covers basic science principles, weighting 6.0 percent of the total score. It explores underlying physiological and pathological concepts that are highly relevant to interventional cardiology practice.

This domain examines anatomy, anatomic variants, and anatomic pathology, contributing 6.0 percent to the exam. It focuses on structural variations and pathological findings found within cardiovascular tissues.

This domain addresses pharmacology, representing 12.0 percent of the test. It reviews therapeutic agents, dosage requirements, and drug interactions associated with various interventional medical treatments across clinical practice environments.
This domain focuses on cardiac imaging and assessment, accounting for 9.0 percent of the exam. It evaluates diagnostic imaging modalities and image interpretation methods used in patient assessment.

This domain covers miscellaneous topics, comprising 6.0 percent of the evaluation. It includes additional clinical subjects and specific practice areas relevant to interventional cardiology professionals preparing for board certification.

editorial.exam_day_guidance: Manage your 600-minute testing time carefully across all 220 questions. Pace yourself to address each domain according to its respective percentage weight, and check with American Board of Internal Medicine for official testing policies.

editorial.overview: The ABIM Interventional Cardiology certification examination, administered by the American Board of Internal Medicine, extensively measures medical expertise across nine distinct subject domains. Candidates complete exactly 220 questions during an extended 600-minute evaluation covering case selection, procedural techniques, and thorough patient management strategies across diverse clinical healthcare settings for certification.
editorial.preparation_strategy: Extensively review the nine distinct exam domains, focusing intently on specific procedural weights such as twenty percent for case selection and twenty percent for procedural techniques. Practice clinical scenarios involving coronary complications, pharmacology, and imaging assessments to adequately prepare for all 220 questions during your study period.
editorial.who_should_take: Cardiologists and medical professionals seeking board certification in interventional cardiology. Candidates require clinical experience in catheter-based procedures, patient assessment, and the management of coronary and noncoronary cardiovascular diseases.
